newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK January public sector deficit.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK January public sector deficit.

text.p: Following is a list of reactions to UK public sector debt repayment data published at 0930 GMT. The figures showed a debt repayment of 5.818 billion pounds in January. Privatisation costs totalled 60 million stg. Economists had forecast a 3.5 billion stg repayment.
"It's much better than expected and will help the gilt market. There's now a chance of a modest undershoot of the government's target this year. I suspect it's down to corporate tax receipts.

"It is pretty good and raises the chances of an undershoot of the government's PSBR target although one must always be very careful about the last minute spending surge in March, particularly ahead of an election. What will be interesting is to what extent this derives from a strong surge in revenues. If that is the case then it confirms the economy remains very strong."

"The UK public finance figures were much better than had been expected. This is a month where there are heavy tax receipts from the corporate sector. An increase is probably related to the improvement in economic condictions and the recovery in corporate profits. Overall, receipts were up 12.3 percent on the same month last year. Expenditure was steady. The cumulative deficit, when privatisation receipts are excluded, shows a near 30 percent fall and suggests the government is well on the way to surpassing its 26.4 billion target."

"Those numbers are obviously positive for the (gilt) market and likely to keep the supportive tone today. There are signs of strength in the economy but it looks like the Chancellor will meet his target. On the fundamental side, you could argue that gilts are a bit of a sell but that is not what the market are concentrating on right now."
